## Shaper

A shaper was a type of psion who specialized in the metacreativity discipline of psionics, honing their skills in drawing ectoplasm or matter from the Astral Plane to conjure solid and semi-solid projections of armor or weapons, as well as animated astral constructs. They were equivalent to the conjurers of arcane magic.

Personality
Shapers were typically very outgoing people, eager to make new friends and acquaintances, but due a perfectionist nature they could be temperamental whenever they were working on crafts. Those who specialized particularly in the making of constructs tended to have a manipulative streak, while those who focused on the manipulation of ectoplasm tended to be very easygoing and malleable.

Activities
Among the six classes of psions, shapers were the most artistically inclined, viewing the world as a canvas just waiting for their mental brush to paint. Even when not using their powers, shapers busied themselves with acts of creation, whether it be whittling the wood for some instruments, repairing armor, crafting all manner of items from crystals, or crafting chemicals and reagents like an alchemist.

Abilities
Shapers almost exclusively utilized powers that fell within the purview of the metacreativity discipline. Their specialization in this discipline allowed shapers to unlock a suite of powers that were unknown to other psions. These powers were as followed – astral construct, astral seed, crystallize, ectoplasmic cocoon and mass ectoplasmic cocoon, greater concealing amorpha, genesis, hail of crystals, psionic fabricate and greater psionic fabricate, psionic minor creation, psionic repair damage, quintessence, and true creation.

In the years following the Spellplague, almost all shapers exhibited the powers psionic minor creation and shaped consciousness.

They often created constructs to fight on their behalf and sought to use their powers in creative ways. To some, the creation of animated constructs was considered the cornerstone of being a shaper.

While some kept a mental list of preconstructed constructs to manifest on a moment's notice, other shapers took a creative bent to their astral constructs, preferring to craft each uniquely as needed. Some shapers even had a specific form of astral construct that they favored above all others.

Possessions
While traditionally psionics users such as shapers didn't need any physical tools or weaponry to practice their discipline, following the Spellplague they began using implements to enhance their abilities. Typically these took the form of orbs and staves, through which they would channel their psionic energy into powers.

Notable Shapers
 Daltim Flamefist, a Halruaan shaper and fire elementalist who commanded a psionic mercenary company known as the Destroyers.
 The Imperator, a massive grell shaper that lived deep within the Vast Swamp.
 Theldir Whitemoon, a sun elf shaper and member of the Kaliesh'erai.

## Shadowcrawler

Shadowcrawlers were a species of cunning subterranean predatory creatures that resembled an uncanny mixture of a cat and spider, believed to be spawned by some magical experiment gone awry.

Description
These hybrid monsters possessed fur-covered feline bodies with eight legs. The fur was ebony in color, short and soft. Their bodies,  in length and standing  tall, appeared to be segmented, separated by sets of shoulders. Each leg ended in a cat-like paw crowned with retractible feline claws. Notably, a shadowcrawler's face was somewhat longer than that of any mundane feline. Their tail was that of a cat.

Behavior
Being intelligent creatures, shadowcrawlers were capable of learning and speaking languages; however, only ten percent of the total population bothered to learn Common or another local tongue. Any language they spoke sounded guttural. Shadowcrawlers did not have their own language.

Abilities
Like spiders, they could move across walls and ceilings normally. Additionally, they almost completely blended into darkness, remaining invisible and silent, easily surprising even the most attentive opponents. However, their ability to phase through walls and other solid matter made them truly dangerous and devious hunters. When phasing through stone, they remained completely undetected by any non-magical means.

The phasing also made them vulnerable to the phase door spell. If it was cast on a shadowcrawler as it was phasing through matter, it immediately killed the monster.

Combat
Being feline and spider in nature, shadowcrawlers were patient and sly hunters, capable of laying in wait for hours at a time or spending prolonged periods of time tracking and staling worthy prey. They targeted groups of humanoids, animals, or unwitting adventurers and waited for a straggler to fall behind. They never targeted creatures bigger than an average human. One of their favorite ambush spots was the ceiling behind a door.

When in open combat, they attacked a single prey by standing on four hind legs, slashing with four front paws, and attempting to lay deadly bites. If at least two of the claw swipes connected with the prey, shadowcrawlers attempted to give them a deadly crushing hug and drag the prey away to be consumed. A hugged victim then was bit while still remaining restrained, as a shadowcrawler drained and devoured their blood.

If hurt, shadowcrawlers tried to escape by phasing through walls and floors, only to reappear later, pouncing from another wall, floor, or ceiling.

Ecology
A shadowcrawler was a solitary beast that harbored hatred towards all other living things. They laired in dry subterranean locations, leaving the lair to hunt during night or day. They were not sensitive to daylight but preferred to remain in darkness. A shadowcrawler's lair was a small dug-out hollow lined with fur in which it slept. Shadowcrawlers were aggressive and light sleepers, hunting, killing, and driving away any creature weaker than it from the surrounding territory. If a bigger and stronger predator appeared within the territory, shadowcrawlers departed without a fight. They attacked creatures of all types but preferred to consume mammalian blood.

Shadowcrawlers mated approximately once per four years. A creature would embark on a mate search, echoing its yowling throughout caves and tunnels. Once mated, shadowcrawlers part ways once again. A fetus gestated for three months, after which a female shadowcrawler laid an egg sack in a secure and hidden spot. A month later, the sack exploded in a litter of two to twelve shadowkittens. The young scattered and went their own way; most were killed before reaching maturity and even before being capable of defending themselves effectively. The babes reached maturity in a year, but only one or two survived from the entire litter.

History
In the mid-14 century DR, shadowcrawlers were found inhabiting tunnels underneath the castle of Darkhold, the lair of the Zhentarim. They were unleashed on the subterranean levels by Varalla the lich. In a battle between the lich and her enemies, the Black Network, the tunnels were accidentally sealed off from the rest of Darkhold, leaving shadowcrawlers to hunt in peace.

## Shandathe Llaerin

Shandathe Llaerin, "the Shadow" was a coinlass of Hastarl in the early 3 century DR. She was married to local baker Hannibur through the mid-3 century DR together.

Description
Shandathe was considered the most beautiful woman in all of Hastarl, with deep, dark eyes.

Personality
She was certainly not above helping out in a mean prank.

Abilities
She was able to get in and out of places with uncanny quiet.

Possessions
Of note, she had a rather fancy dagger.

Relationships
She married Hannibur, a local baker.

History
On  at The Kissing Wench, a tavern, Shandathe Llaerin propositioned her services to a local thief of Hastarl, Eladar the Dark, who was secretly Prince Elminster Aumar. Before they came to an arrangement, local dandy Jansibal Otharr outbid him and nearly had his guards start a confrontation. After the situation was de-escalated, Shandathe's servicing of Jansibal was interrupted again, this time by Eladar and his friend Farl, who knocked out Jansibal, and borrowed one of Shandathe's earrings, which they used to convince another local dandy, Thelorn Selemban, that Shandathe would know him, unsatisfied by Jansibal. Shandathe complied, rather enthusiastically. Afterwards, to remove suspicion from her, they took her and hurled her through the bedroom window of a local baker, Hannibur, despite her rising wariness.

She started seeing Hannibur on the evenings after that, and after a while, they got married. Eladar the Dark brought them a number of coins for their wedding night.

Later in, Shandathe was kidnapped from their bakery by the men of King Belaur Aumar, for the king had caught sight of her face and fancied her. However, the King was prevented from having carnal contact with her because his castle was besieged at that precise point, requiring him to move to a safer location within the castle. She was later rescued by Myrjala Talithyn and reunited with her husband upon the death of King Belaur.

Rumors & Legends
Eladar the Dark noted some time after hurling Shandathe inside Hannibur's home that no word of the meeting between Shandathe and Hannibur had spread, which made him wonder why.

On, Elminster Aumar was mind-called to Druindar's Rock: Delmuth Echorn lured him in with an image of Shandathe bound and tortured, begging him to save her. This was but a ruse unrelated to the real Shandathe.

Shamasar and his dragonborn troops were no ordinary soldiers: they used combinations of their breath weapons to control battlefields with fire and poison, and just a few of them were sufficient to stall an entire army.

History

In the late 1460s DR, Shamasar was party to a plot by Valeanne to smuggle Princess Amaranth out of the Sarifal capital of Karador in order to protect her from the wrath of her half-sister, High Lady Ordalf. Shamasar brought five of his dragonborn soldiers with him on their pre-dawn ride to Crane Point, including Gesh and Haroon. Upon nearing their destination, they were attacked by a company of drow, and Shamasar and his underlings dutifully sacrificed themselves to buy Valeanne as much time as they could. Shamasar was torn from his mount by drow after sustaining many arrows and single-handedly cutting down two driders as they leapt onto him.

After his death, it was believed that Valeanne had bribed or otherwise compelled Shamasar and his guards to betray the High Lady.

## Shadow-corrupted water elemental

The shadow-corrupted water elemental was an unfortunate elemental that dwelled in the ruins of Beckside Castle in the late 15 century DR.

Abilities

The elemental was much more powerful than others of its kind, and could wield the negative energy powers that it had been infused with.

History

When the Shadovar and Harpers pursued a Nether Scroll at Beckside Castle, the dark wizard Keldan Shadeskein bound one of the local water elementals to his will, infused it with shadows, and tied its life and his into a defensive barrier that protected Gaston Wyrst while he worked on obtaining the Scroll. The elemental was imbued with fell energies and left in the flooded basement of the castle, where Harper agents eventually found it and mercifully destroyed it, opening the way forward.

## Shannyth River Valley

The Shannyth River Valley, also known as the Shannyth Valley, was an idyllic and fertile river valley through which the Shannyth River flowed on the island of Moray in the Moonshae Isles.

Geography
The valley lay in northern Moray where the river approached the Sea of Moonshae. It was a low and verdant valley through which travelers followed a rutted dirt path that barely qualified as a road, but was well-worn enough for carts to travel at speed.

Flora & Fauna
The valley was filled with lush grasses and colorful wildflowers of blues, reds and yellows. It was home to bees, butterflies, leprechauns, sprites, and small mammals.

Inhabitants
During the height of the Kingdom of Moray, the Valley hosted the densest concentration of Ffolk settlers scattered along its length from Dynnegall in the south to Moray-town in the north. These Ffolk spoke of the fertile valley in reverent, almost mystical terms.

## Shattering (Calimshan)

The Shattering was the magical destruction of the Maridlands, Ajhuutal, and Ajhuu himself, culminating the Steam War with Calim and the Calim Empire.

Description
After years of war against his rebellious vassal, in  Calim brought together his dao allies and his magical artifacts from the Great Arrival (believed to include the scepter of Calim) and performed a great magical ritual that sundered the city of Ajhuutal and sent the surrounding area into the Shining Sea. Though this killed Ajhuu and ended the rebellion, Calim's fury at the rebellion led him to empower the ritual far beyond its needs, causing the destructive earthquakes to spread far beyond Ajhuutal along the coast and inland. Where before the coastline was a near-straight line from the River of Ice to the Alimir Mountains, the Shattering tore it apart and caused the sea to rush in, transforming half the length of the Maridflow from a pleasant river valley to a cliff-lined bay of jagged rocks, and doing the same further south to the foothills of the Alimir Peaks. It also blasted and reshaped the westwards Quag and Volomir Rivers, turning it from the most fertile floodplain in the Calim Empire into a half-bitten bay and a brackish swamp later known as the Spider Swamp.

Though he had destroyed a significant portion of his own empire in the process, the Shattering was enough for Calim to claim victory over the rebellious vassal Ajhuu, who was presumed dead from the Shattering.

## Shoonach Conflagration

The Shoonach Conflagration, or the Great Fires of Shoonach, was the intentional arson and destruction of Shoonach's Imperial City, capital of the Shoon Imperium, at the hand of Prince Strohm of Tethyr. Along with the death of Emperor Amahl Shoon VII, this marked the end of the already teetering Shoon Imperium.

History
After forming a sizable rebel army and taking the throne of Tethyr from the abdicating King Priam Tornamn in 449 DR, King Silvyr Ithal proceeded to march on Shoonach, reaching the city in late Uktar. After a tenday of skirmishing and fighting, the two sides declared a truce and a challenge of single combat at the Taraqin Arena between Silvyr and Amahl VII on the Feast of the Moon. To the dismay of his followers Silvyr was slain by poison and the Tethyrian army was ambushed and slaughtered as well. For the next month Amahl and his forces celebrated their victory, believing that they had utterly vanquished the rebellious forces of Tethyr. Unfortunately for them, the clever Prince Strohm had hidden and protected much of the Tethyrian army, and proceeded to infiltrate part of them into the city under cover of the celebrations. On Hammer 30 of 450 DR King Strohm launched his own attack on the city, revealing his army encamped outside the city in concert with the forces within, having used the Imperial City's sewers, the tombs of Debukkher, and the slave population as cover (they were also joined by many slaves eager to see the overthrow of Shoon). With the assistance of his human and elven companions, Strohm assaulted the Imperial Mount and as the night turned to Midwinter, Emperor Amahl Shoon VII was slain. Thus Midwinter was celebrated as the Day of Freedom for many peoples of Faerûn as the breaking of Shoon subjugation.

After a day of fierce fighting with the remnants of the Shoon defenses and Amahl's heirs, Strohm's forces set fires around the Imperial City and let it burn. In the conflagration that followed the Imperial City was razed, killing the entire remaining royal family and the vast majority of the generals and officials who had been responsible for the running of the empire. Four days into the disaster, the great blue dragon Iryklathagra (nemesis of Shoon VII) arrived and negotiated with Strohm, coming to the agreement that she could loot the choicest magical treasures from the Palace Mount and in return never again hunt in Tethyr. Strohm left the ruined city and returned to Tethyr, what remained of the city's vaults and treasuries were looted by opportunists, and the Shoon Imperium collapsed in the years that followed.

## Shaleel Warehouses

Shaleel Warehouses were a trio of busy and well-guarded warehouses owned by the Harrowcoaster Coster company in the 14 century DR, located in Harrowdale Town in the Dalelands.

Location
Shaleel Warehouses stood on Cart Street, just north of Moonside Lane, and west of The Harrow Plow pier.

Structure
The three all-stone warehouses were decorated with the Harrowcoaster Coster insignia, the same image that decorated all of their shipping crates and packages: a circle of gold coins encircling a ship with its sail up high.

Services
When Harrowcoaster Coster imported goods into Harrowdale, they were repackaged and stored in Shaleel Warehouses until the coaster received sale orders for the goods to be shipped. The goods were imported without corresponding pre-orders from the buyers—a risky strategy that often paid off in the speed of order fulfillment. The selection of stored goods was wide, including such exotics as silk dancer's costumes from Calimshan.

## Shikimi

Shikimi was a wood elf rogue and spy from Wa in Kara-Tur. She served a lord in Kozakura, then protected his son on the Sword Coast in the late 15 century DR.

History
Shikimi was raised in a hidden village of elves located somewhere in Wa. On behalf of the village, her family's mission was to spy on the human world outside. To this end, Shikimi went to Kozakura, where she operated as a spy serving a human samurai family. In time, she felt a secret yet pure love for the head of the family.

But the machinations of followers of Asmodeus led to the family being destroyed by a rival samurai family. Shikimi could only save the lord's son, Tatsuwaka-maru, from being killed. The pair fled, along with Oni-guma, a warrior who also served the young lord, but were pursued by the Asmodeus-worshipers. They were aided by Kugetsu and Hakuroku-bou, a pair of mystics who'd come seeking to thwart the followers of Asmodeus.

They escaped into the mountains, but passed through a teleportation circle that unexpectedly spirited them all to the far side of Faerûn, to the Sword Coast.While page 1 of The Oni's Right Hand says they escaped using a teleportation circle that malfunctioned, the pregenerated character biographies instead says they went into the mountains and passed through a portal.

Circa 1491 DR,The Oni's Right Hand is intended to be a starting quest for Dragon of Icespire Peak, which is presumed to be set around 1491 DR. the five companions arrived in the town of Phandalin, where they may have become caught up in stopping the oni Jadou-maru from recovering the Glove of Oni Claw at the Lionshield Coster.

Relationships
Shikimi was bound to protect the young lord Tatsuwaka-maru, the son of the man she loved.

Description
At age 145, she stood 152 centimeters (5 feet) tall and weighed 42 kilograms (93 pounds).

Personality

Shikimi was loyal to her friends above all, and did not care so much for ideals or strangers.

She blamed herself for a mistake that led to the death of her lord, and vowed to never repeat it. Thus, she was always cautious, sizing up a place upon entering and laying plans in case things went bad.

When Shikimi told a lie, she had a tell that could reveal her.

Possessions
Shikimi was armed with a short sword, two daggers, and a short bow, with twenty arrows in her quiver. She wore leather armor but also had ninja attire. She was also equipped with thieves' tools, a backpack, belt pouch, and a set of adventuring and burglary gear, including a bag of ball bearings,  of string,  of hempen rope,  five candles, a crowbar, a bell, a hammer and ten pitons, a hooded lantern with two flasks of oil and a tinderbox, rations for five days, and a waterskin.

Appendix
Background
Shikimi is a pre-generated character released on the Dungeons & Dragons Japan website to accompany the free learn-to-play adventure, The Oni's Right Hand. Her personality details are stock traits from pages 129–130 of Player's Handbook 5th edition (2014). According to creator Masaki Yanagida, her name means 'sacred anise tree', a highly toxic plant used for making incense.

She was voiced by Tomori Kusunoki in a promotional video.

## Shev'aal

Shev'aal was a giant spider that lived in the Ziggurat beneath the Temple of Lolth atop the city of Sschindylryn in the 1480s DR.

History
During the Sschindylryn invasion of Eveningstar, Shev'aal lived in the dedicated spider quarters within the Ziggurat, enjoying a diet of slaves. Despite this lifestyle, Shev'aal was still a morally uncompromised beast.

## Shadow wolf

Shadow wolves were powerful wolf-like creatures native to the Shadowfell.

Description
Shadow wolves were enormous in size, compared to their mundane counterparts from the Prime Material plane. They looked like creatures made out of shadows, surrounded by an eerie dark mist, with their eyes glowing with red malevolence.

History
In the late 15 century DR, shadow wolves were known to be summoned to the Prime by the mages of Returned Netheril. These summoned creatures were used for their savage strength on the field of battle and as obedient mounts. Some adventurers ended up using shadow wolves as their mounts as well.
